Recombinant cysteine-less (C459A) perfringolysin O (PFO) with N-terminal His-tag was supplied by Michael Parker. The protocols for expression and purification of recombinant PFO C459A have been described previously ( Shepard et al. , 1998 ; Wade et al. , 2015 ). Production and handling of PFO should be done in accordance with local occupational health and safety regulations for handling toxins. Store frozen in small aliquots at -80 °C. After thawing an aliquot, store at room temperature for up to two months. The protein loses activity when stored at 4 °C or during repeated freeze-thaw cycles. Option
Alternatively, streptolysin O (SLO) (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: S

can be used for permeabilization of viral particles (unpublished data). Handling of SLO should be done in accordance with local occupational health and safety regulations for handling toxins. Dissolve the protein in PBS containing 2 mM TCEP to give a concentration of ~8 μM, prepare small aliquots, freeze in liquid nitrogen and store frozen at -80 °C. Thaw a fresh aliquot on the day of use. Unlike PFO C459A, wild type SLO loses activity in solution as a result of oxidation (disulfide formation). steps.title: Prepare cell culture media
steps.instruction: Make Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10 % (v/v) fetal bovine serum (FBS). Store at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Transfect HEK-293T cells for VLPs
steps.instruction: In a 15 ml conical tube, mix 6.6 µg pNL4.3‑iGFP‑Env plasmid, 3.3 µg psPAX2 plasmid, and 60 µl of 1 mg ml⁻¹ PEI‑max in 0.9 % (w/v) NaCl to a final volume of 500 µl. Incubate 30 min at room temperature. Remove medium from a T25 flask of HEK‑293T cells, wash with 1× PBS, add ~1 ml 1× trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 5 min at 37 °C, then add fresh culture medium to stop digestion. Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 ml tube, count cells, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min at room temperature, discard supernatant, and resuspend to 7 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹. Add 1 ml cell suspension to the DNA‑PEI mix, incubate 5 min at room temperature, then dropwise add the mixture to a 10 cm² dish containing 6.5 ml culture medium. Shake gently, incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Collect and clarify virus supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant into a 15 ml conical tube, centrifuge 2,100 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, transfer the cleared supernatant (~7 ml) to a new tube.

steps.title: Optional fluorescence verification of VLPs
steps.instruction: Dilute supernatant 1:100 in PBS, spinoculate 200 µl onto a poly‑L‑lysine‑coated glass‑bottom 96‑well plate at 1,200 × g for 60 min at 4 °C, image with a 60× objective, count fluorescent dots in ≥4 fields, calculate particles per well and per µl.

steps.title: Biotinylate viral particles
steps.instruction: Dissolve ~1 mg EZ‑Link™ Sulfo‑NHS‑LC‑LC‑Biotin in 1 ml HBS pH 7.5. Add this solution to the cleared virus supernatant, incubate 90 min at 4 °C in the dark with gentle rotation.

steps.title: Equilibrate SEC column
steps.instruction: Connect a HiPrep 16/60 Sephacryl S‑500 HR column to an FPLC system. Filter all buffers through 0.2 µm membranes and degas. Replace the column’s storage solution with 2 column volumes (CV) of purified water, then equilibrate with 2 CV of HBS pH 7.5 at 1 ml min⁻¹. Start the equilibration the day before virus collection (≈8 h required).

steps.title: Run size exclusion chromatography
steps.instruction: Load ~6.5 ml biotinylated virus onto the column using a 10‑ml superloop at 0.5 ml min⁻¹. Elute with HBS pH 7.5, collecting 1 ml fractions at a flow rate of 0.5 ml min⁻¹ until 1.5 CV have passed (≈6 h). Monitor absorbance at 280 nm.

steps.title: Collect viral fractions and store
steps.instruction: Combine fractions 34‑39 (or C10‑D3) that contain the first small peak. Store purified biotinylated particles at 4 °C for up to 7 days or aliquot 200‑500 µl and freeze at –80 °C (no liquid‑N₂ flash freezing). Thaw on ice before use.

steps.title: Grow BL21 E. coli for CypA
steps.instruction: Inoculate 5 ml LB + 100 µg ml⁻¹ ampicillin with a single BL21 (DE3) colony harboring pETMCSI‑hCypA; grow overnight at 37 °C, 180 rpm. Use this starter to inoculate 500 ml fresh LB + ampicillin (100 µg ml⁻¹) with 5 ml starter. Grow at 37 °C, 180 rpm until OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.6.

steps.title: Induce CypA expression
steps.instruction: Add IPTG to a final concentration of 1 mM, continue shaking 3 h at 37 °C, 180 rpm.

steps.title: Lyse cells and clarify lysate
steps.instruction: Pellet cells 6,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in cold lysis buffer (15 ml per 500 ml pellet; composition: 25 mM HEPES pH 7.6, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % w/v NaN₃, 1 mg ml⁻¹ lysozyme, complete protease inhibitor). Sonicate on ice (50 % duty, setting 3, 15 s on/15 s off, 12 cycles). Centrifuge lysate 43,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C, filter supernatant through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Anion exchange purification of CypA
steps.instruction: Connect two 5 ml HiTrap Q HP columns in tandem. Wash each with 5 CV AIEX buffer A (25 mM HEPES pH 7.6, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃), then 5 CV AIEX buffer B (same as A plus 1.5 M NaCl). Equilibrate with 5 CV AIEX buffer A at 5 ml min⁻¹. Load the clarified lysate, collect flow‑through in 1 ml fractions, continue eluting with an additional ~5 ml AIEX buffer A. Identify CypA‑containing fractions by reducing SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Adjust pH and remove aggregates
steps.instruction: Adjust pooled flow‑through to pH 5.8 with 1 % v/v acetic acid. Centrifuge 43,000 × g for 1 h at 4 °C, keep the supernatant.

steps.title: Cation exchange purification of CypA
steps.instruction: Load supernatant onto a 5 ml HiTrap SP HP column pre‑washed with 5 CV CIEX buffer A (25 mM sodium phosphate pH 5.8, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃) and equilibrated with the same buffer at 1 ml min⁻¹. Wash with 2 CV CIEX buffer A, then elute with a linear 0‑1 M NaCl gradient (0‑100 % CIEX buffer B) over 20 CV at 5 ml min⁻¹. Collect fractions; CypA elutes at 20‑25 % buffer B.

steps.title: Dialyze and concentrate CypA
steps.instruction: Dialyze CypA‑containing fractions against CypA storage buffer (25 mM MOPS pH 6.6, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃) for three × 4 h using 3.5 kDa MWCO tubing. Determine protein concentration by Bradford assay (BSA standard). If needed, concentrate with an Amicon‑15 Ultra 10 kDa filter to a final concentration of 100‑300 µM (1.8‑5.4 mg ml⁻¹). Aliquot and flash‑freeze in liquid N₂; store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Label CypA with Alexa 568
steps.instruction: Exchange CypA into PBS + 0.1 mM TCEP using a Zeba desalting spin column to remove DTT. Mix CypA with a 4‑fold molar excess of Alexa‑Fluor 568‑C5‑maleimide (e.g., 130 µl of 100 µM CypA with 5 µl of 10 mM dye) in PBS pH 7.4, incubate 10 min at room temperature. Quench with 1 M DTT to a final 10 mM. Remove free dye by a second Zeba spin into AF568‑CypA storage buffer (50 mM Tris pH 8, 20 % v/v glycerol, 1 mM DTT).

steps.title: Determine concentration and DOL
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 280 nm (A₂₈₀) and at the dye maximum (~578 nm, A_dye) using a NanoDrop. Calculate CypA concentration: c = (A₂₈₀ – CF × A_dye)/ε_CypA, where CF = 0.45 and ε_CypA = 8730 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹. Calculate degree of labeling: DOL = (A_dye/ε_dye)/c, with ε_dye = 91300 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹. Expected DOL ≈ 1. Prepare 2‑4 µl aliquots at ~100 µM, flash‑freeze, store at –40 °C.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS microfluidic devices
steps.instruction: Mix 30 ml PDMS elastomer and curing agent (10:1 w/v). Degas under vacuum 20 min, pour over a silicon wafer mold, cure overnight at 70 °C. Remove cured PDMS, cut into squares fitting the magnetic imaging chamber, punch 1.0 mm inlet/outlet holes with a Harris Uni‑Core, clean by immersing 10 min each in water, 100 % isopropanol, and water. Dry with lint‑free tissue and store with channels up.

steps.title: Clean glass coverslips
steps.instruction: Place 25 mm round coverslips in a holder. Sonicate 30 min in absolute ethanol, then 30 min in 1 M NaOH. Rinse three times by gently shaking in ultrapure water, wick excess water with lint‑free tissue, then dry in a heated oven ≥30 min. Use immediately or store in a desiccator (≤1 month).

steps.title: Assemble microfluidic flow cell
steps.instruction: Plasma‑treat a cleaned coverslip and a PDMS device (channels up) for 3 min in an air plasma cleaner. Align the PDMS block onto the center of the coverslip, channels facing the glass, and press gently for a uniform seal. Place the assembled device in an oven at 70 °C for 15 min. Use immediately or store (≤2 weeks).

steps.title: Prepare inlet and outlet tubing
steps.instruction: Cut 5‑7 cm pieces for inlets (single‑use) and 10‑13 cm pieces for outlets. Attach a blunted 1 mm OD needle to each outlet end. Rinse reusable tubing with distilled water using a syringe, then dry by drawing air through.

steps.title: Functionalize flow channel surface
steps.instruction: Using a P20 pipette, inject 1 mg ml⁻¹ biotinylated poly‑L‑lysine‑g‑poly‑ethylene glycol solution into a flow channel until it exits the opposite port (~3 µl). Incubate 30 min at room temperature. Mount the device in a magnetic chamber, connect inlet/outlet tubing, and place inlet tubing in a microcentrifuge tube containing ultrapure water (keep inlets immersed).

steps.title: Streptavidin block and rinse
steps.instruction: Draw 0.2 mg ml⁻¹ streptavidin in blocking buffer into the channel via the outlet syringe, incubate 15 min (≈100 µl fills five channels). Keep inlets immersed to avoid air exposure. Rinse with HBS pH 7.5 (~200 µl per channel). Keep channels filled with solution for the remainder of the day.

steps.title: Load biotinylated viral particles
steps.instruction: Inject purified biotinylated virus in HBS pH 7.5 at 25 µl min⁻¹ until ~1,000 particles per field of view are observed (typically 30‑100 µl). Focus on the channel center; fluorescent particles should appear as diffraction‑limited spots.

steps.title: Wash unbound particles
steps.instruction: Flush the channel with 50‑100 µl HBS pH 7.5 at 65 µl min⁻¹ to remove unbound virus.

steps.title: Prepare CypA paint solution
steps.instruction: In HBS pH 7.0 make a 40 µl solution containing 200 nM perfringolysin O (PFO), 0.5‑1 µM AF568‑CypA, 2 mM Trolox, 2.5 mM protocatechuic acid (PCA), and 0.25 U ml⁻¹ protocatechuate‑3,4‑dioxygenase (PCD). Adjust pH to 7.0 (PFO is less active above pH 7.5).

steps.title: Inject paint and start TIRF imaging
steps.instruction: Inject 30 µl of the CypA paint solution at 65 µl min⁻¹ while simultaneously beginning TIRF acquisition. Use 488 nm excitation for GFP and 561 nm for AF568. Set laser power density to ~1 W cm⁻² at the objective, exposure 20 ms. Record 800 frames at 1 frame s⁻¹ for short assays (≈13.3 min) or at 1 frame 6 s⁻¹ for long assays (≈80 min).

steps.title: Repeat assay in remaining channels
steps.instruction: Perform the surface functionalization, virus loading, washing, paint injection, and imaging steps (B5‑B11) for each additional flow channel of the device.

steps.title: Single‑molecule photobleaching assay
steps.instruction: Mount a clean coverslip in a magnetic chamber, add ~300 µl 0.02 mg ml⁻¹ BSA, incubate 2 min, then remove and wash with HBS pH 7. Add 10 nM AF568‑CypA in HBS pH 7, incubate 3‑5 min, wash with HBS pH 7. Place the chamber on the microscope stage and acquire photobleaching movies with 561 nm excitation at the same laser power used for the uncoating assay, using 200 ms exposures until ~150 frames have been recorded and most single molecules are bleached.

steps.title: Prepare buffer recipes
steps.instruction:
Prepare the following solutions as listed:
- HBS (pH 7.0 or 7.5): 50 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl, adjust pH.
- Lysis buffer: 25 mM HEPES pH 7.6, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃, 1 mg ml⁻¹ lysozyme, complete protease inhibitor.
- AIEX buffer A: 25 mM HEPES pH 7.6, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃.
- AIEX buffer B: AIEX A + 1.5 M NaCl.
- CIEX buffer A: 25 mM sodium phosphate pH 5.8, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃.
- CIEX buffer B: CIEX A + 1 M NaCl.
- CypA storage buffer: 25 mM MOPS pH 6.6, 1 mM DTT, 0.02 % NaN₃.
- AF568‑CypA storage buffer: 50 mM Tris pH 8, 20 % v/v glycerol, 1 mM DTT.
- Blocking buffer: 20 mM Tris pH 7.5, 2 mM EDTA, 50 mM NaCl, 0.03 % NaN₃, 0.025 % Tween 20, 0.2 mg ml⁻¹ BSA.
